findings.message: CWE-706 — `dadaia import --workspace <path>` / `dadaia export --workspace <path>` re-resolve an explicit path through the ancestor walk and write into a parent workspace (cli/commands/import_.py:30, cli/commands/export.py:29 -> core/workspace_resolver.py:57-66).
findings.detail_md:
In range: f4bf7e0b (T-046-31) introduced `container.build_import_service(resolve_workspace_root(workspace))`; `resolve_workspace_root` walks up from the given path to the first ancestor holding `.dadaia/states/spec_contexts.json` and never applies the `.dadaia/` boundary that `resolve_workspace_root_for_init(explicit=True)` / `_is_nested_inside_dotdadaia` (workspace_resolver.py:97-124) added for bug `ancestor-walk-workspace-root-silent-mistarget` (HIGH, resolved 3084f832, scoped to init + reports validate).

Reproduced by the predecessor review: `dadaia import --workspace <live>/.dadaia/tmp/security-reviewer/20260904/noinit <file>` (an uninitialized dir) exited 0 and registered two DEAD records (`thief`/slug `alpha`, `good`/slug `good-repo`) in the LIVE workspace registry (13 contexts); reverted with `dadaia context delete thief` and `dadaia context delete good` (registry back to 11, no `repos/` residue). Impact is bounded by `SpecContextService.register`: only allowlisted, unowned slugs land, as DEAD records, nothing on disk. Bug-history reading: same symptom as the resolved HIGH, on a second verb pair — the earlier fix was verb-local, which is the recurrence signature.

Delta 637059d2..efd58d33: registered in 02aac90f as BUGS.jsonl `import-export-workspace-flag-re-resolves-through-ancestor-walk` (LOW, open, reported_by security-reviewer, redacted). Production code unchanged in the delta; finding status otherwise unchanged.
findings.fix_recommendation: Arm B, non-blocking; registration done (02aac90f). Structural fix (deletion-shaped): one resolver that honors an explicit path as authoritative (raise WorkspaceNotInitializedError when it lacks the sentinel) and applies the `.dadaia/` boundary for every verb; delete the init-only `resolve_workspace_root_for_init` variant so the rule has one home. RED test: `import --workspace <uninitialized dir nested under a workspace's .dadaia/tmp>` must exit 1 and write nothing.

findings.message: CWE-59/CWE-61 — a symlinked zone root (e.g. `.dadaia/handoff -> ../repos/<victim>`) is classified `canon` by the top-level scan and never surfaced (features/spec_context/doctor.py:389-391 `_scan_dadaia_top`: `entry.is_dir()` follows the link).
findings.detail_md:
Pre-existing, not widened by this range; the predecessor's observation confirmed. With `_entries` (doctor.py:305-314) refusing to walk a symlinked root, the read side is inert: reproduced — `dadaia doctor --json` on a scratch workspace with `.dadaia/handoff -> ../repos/victim` (containing `old.txt` aged 3 days) yielded `issues: []`, no finding naming `old.txt`, no finding on `handoff`, compliance 10/13; `dadaia doctor --fix --expired-only` (the SessionStart lane) seeded only the missing `agentic`/`hooks` zones, `old.txt` survived and the symlink remained. The lane cannot act on it today. Residual: a scan that reports the zone as canon hides a redirected zone root for every later reader (`--fix` seeding, future zone-level deletion, any writer that trusts the zone path).

Delta 637059d2..efd58d33: doctor.py untouched; unchanged.
findings.fix_recommendation: Non-blocking. In `_scan_dadaia_top`, classify `entry.is_symlink()` as SLOP with detail `(symlink)` so `--fix` routes it through `_remove` (doctor.py:596-603), which unlinks a symlink and never follows it; one-line change on the classification branch, no new path. Pin with the existing `test_a_symlinked_zone_root_is_never_walked` parametrization extended to assert one `WS-dadaia-slop` finding on the zone entry.

findings.message: CWE-59 defense-in-depth — `_remove_dead_repo` (doctor.py:537) admits `repos/<slug>` when it is a symlink to a sibling INSIDE repos/; the refusal then rests on `shutil.rmtree` raising on a symlink, reported as `INV-5: skipped 'repos/linkin' (errno None: None)`.
findings.detail_md: Reproduced by the predecessor: `repos/linkin -> alpha` (alpha ALIVE) with a poisoned DEAD record `linkin`; `doctor --fix` reported the errno-None skip and `repos/alpha/marker.txt` survived. Safe in CPython, but the guard's stated contract (`resolve().parent == repos/`) is satisfied and the protection is implicit and its message uninformative. Unchanged by the delta (doctor.py untouched).
findings.fix_recommendation: Add `or repo_path.is_symlink()` to the containment predicate at doctor.py:537 so the refusal is explicit and reads `skipped 'repos/<slug>' (symlink)`; extend `test_inv5_fix_never_follows_a_symlinked_repo_dir` with the inside-repos target.

findings.message: INV-5 scan side (doctor.py:211-221) still evaluates `(repos / ctx.repo_slug).exists()` without the fix-side containment predicate: a poisoned record with slug `..` or `.` reports `Context 'x' is dead but repo '..' is on disk` (fixable=True).
findings.detail_md: Report-only false positive on a hand-edited registry (register() no longer admits such slugs); the fix side refuses (`INV-5: skipped 'repos/..' (outside repos/)`, reproduced by the predecessor). No exposure. Unchanged by the delta.
findings.fix_recommendation: Optional: share one containment predicate between the INV-5 scan and `_remove_dead_repo` so the scan reports `(slug resolves outside repos/)` instead of a fixable INV-5.

findings.message: Delta test review — `_age` platform guard and the skipif on `test_symlinks_are_never_followed_and_only_the_link_is_deleted` (tests/unit/test_spec_context_doctor_root.py:77-84, :449-452) assert nothing differently on POSIX and leave the never-follow contract pinned on every platform; recurrence signature noted (second test-local ageing helper to hit the Windows utime gap).
findings.detail_md:
POSIX path: `os.utime in os.supports_follow_symlinks` is True on Linux/macOS, so `_age` issues the byte-identical prior call; the skipif condition is False, the test runs (local: 25 passed, 0 skipped). Windows path: plain `os.utime` follows a link, but every `_age` call outside the gated test receives a regular file or directory (`_age(link)` at :466 is the only link ageing and sits inside the gated test; :660-690 ages `victim`, a regular file, then symlinks the zone root without ageing the link). Contract coverage on Windows after the skip: `test_a_symlinked_zone_root_is_never_walked[True|False]` (:660, unguarded, asserts no finding under the target, target intact, link intact, `actions == []`) and `tests/unit/test_spec_context_doctor.py:228` (INV-5 symlinked repo dir) still exercise `_entries`/`_remove` never following a link; only the unlink-the-link-itself-on-expiry assertion (:476) is Windows-skipped. Windows proof is the CI run on the push: the bug record's `evidence_loop` cites the RED run 33841217321 and POSIX GREEN only; symlink creation on windows-latest is not a new risk (test_spec_context_doctor.py:228, test_presence_gc.py:188, test_scoped_law.py:71-82 already create symlinks unguarded in the same tier and that job's only failures were the 9 NotImplementedError).

Bug history (operator standing order): `retention-sweep-test-uses-windows-unsupported-utime-followsymlinks` (2026-06-25, LOW, resolved b8c40708 by deleting the kwarg in that file's helper; file since deleted with the retention feature) is the first occurrence of this class; the new record declares `caused_by: none` and names the class in `cause`. `grep -rln 'os\.utime' tests/` lists 6 files with 12 call sites and no shared ageing helper — each file re-derives the platform rule. Ledger nit: the record's `evidence_diff` says `+9/-1`; `git diff --numstat 637059d2..HEAD` measures `+11/-1` (the 4-line skipif decorator counted). Record-only.
findings.fix_recommendation: Non-blocking. Deletion-shaped consolidation for a later candidate: one `age(path, epoch)` helper under tests/helpers/ carrying the `os.supports_follow_symlinks` guard, replacing the per-file `_age` helpers and raw `os.utime` calls (6 files); the skipif reason then references the helper. Correct the `evidence_diff` figure on the next touch of the record (mutable governance field).
